recommendation: Keep production QP objective unchanged for first physical posture candidate. Prefer contact-consistent body shift geometry.
reason: At fixed generalized acceleration, stronger rated-torque objective hardly helps standing knees and increases the already-high RL knee in poststop/crouch. Large unrestricted savings come from acceleration tracking error.
potential_future_minimal_change: If separately explored, add optional torque_objective_scale to solve_wbc_qp (default hard limits). Use it ONLY in H/q torque regularizer; keep limits and torque bounds unchanged. Add controller opt-in rated scale [8.3,18,18]*4 and regularization .01 first. Reset warm state on objective changes.
required_tests: Default scale gives same acceleration/force/torque as current solver.
Changing objective scale does not change hard limit, velocity, or slew constraint matrix/bounds.
Rated weights .01 preserve static base tracking error <.1 in real-model standing/crouch.
Asymmetric fixed-acceleration contact test quantifies normalized torque cost and preserves base/contact equations.
All input scales must be finite and positive with scalar or12/batched shape validation.
NumPy/Torch parity and cold/warm reset behavior if solver API modified.
caveats: 62 offline states; no rollout or hardware validation.
All ADMM candidates feasible in these samples, but rated10 had zero converged samples at320 iterations. Feasibility alone does not preserve body support behavior.
Cold ADMM can differ by several Nm from equality-optimal forces even when reported converged; use exact optimum to assess objective benefit and closed-loop warmed solver for deployment.
Pinocchio dynamic torque recomputation using logged acceleration/forces matches six representative601 samples within1.5e-11Nm.
Actual root-origin body linear velocity reconstructed from R.T@world_velocity; result.npz velocity stores COM velocity and is not the WBC input.
